title: Amazon Device Deals Aren’t Great Anymore, but These Are the Ones We’d Still Snag
gist: Amazon raised list prices across Echo, Kindle, Eero and Fire TV devices at the end of August 2026, so fall Prime Big Deal Days (Oct 6-7) discounts are shallower in real terms. Wired's reviewer says the hikes look permanent and flags which devices (Echo Spot, Echo Studio, Ember Artline TV) escaped them.

insights.claim: Amazon raised prices across its Echo, Kindle, Eero and Fire TV device categories at the end of August 2026 with no product improvements, making the same lineup a worse value.
insights.speaker: Nena Farrell
insights.so_what: Consumer hardware pricing power is being exercised at Amazon, a signal for device margins and possible tariff or cost pass-through.
insights.quote: That's thanks to Amazon raising prices across its device categories at the end of August, leaving us with the same product lineup but a worse case to recommend it.

insights.claim: The August price increases appear permanent rather than promotional, so Prime Big Deal Days discounts are measured against a higher base price.
insights.speaker: Nena Farrell
insights.so_what: Headline discount percentages overstate savings; watch Amazon hardware revenue and margin for a structural reset in device pricing.
insights.quote: They do seem to be permanent price changes, though, so if you're certain you want one of these models, this is the best time to buy.
insights.locator: Which Amazon Devices Are on Sale Already

insights.claim: Echo Show 21 rose $100 to $500 and Echo Show 15 rose $50 to $350, the steepest Echo hikes, while the Echo Dot (5th Gen) rose $30 to $80 and the Echo Show 5 rose $10 to $100.
insights.speaker: Nena Farrell
insights.so_what: Larger absolute hikes on premium displays suggest Amazon is testing price elasticity at the high end.

insights.claim: Kindle e-readers rose $30 to $50 across the lineup (Kindle to $150, Paperwhite to $200, Paperwhite Signature to $250, Colorsoft to $290), and Eero 7 Pro rose $100 to $800.
insights.speaker: Nena Farrell
insights.so_what: Price increases of roughly 15-35% on e-readers and routers point to input-cost or margin repair in Amazon's devices unit.
insights.locator: The Amazon Kindle e-reader price changes were

insights.claim: Fire TV Stick 4K Max rose $25 to $85, roughly a 42% jump on its prior $60 price, while Fire TV Stick HD rose only $5 to $40.
insights.speaker: Nena Farrell
insights.so_what: Amazon is monetising its premium streaming tier harder, even though devices usually serve as a subsidised entry to Prime.
insights.locator: the changes to Fire TV devices we recommend were

insights.claim: Sales can be a mind game: a $40 discount on a device that rose $20 weeks earlier is effectively only $20 off the old price.
insights.speaker: Nena Farrell
insights.so_what: Raise-then-discount tactics inflate reported promotion depth while holding realised price, so watch for effective ASP gains in Prime event data.
insights.quote: Its price did increase $20, though, so it feels like it's just $20 off even if it looks like $40.

insights.claim: The Kindle Paperwhite Kids at $170 is only $10 below its prior $180 retail price, and the Kindle Kids at $123 is only $7 below its prior $130.
insights.speaker: Nena Farrell
insights.so_what: Real discounts on several Kindles are single-digit dollars, so unit-volume lifts from Prime events may be weaker than headlines suggest.

insights.claim: The reviewer advises buying Amazon devices only on sale, because sales now apply similar percentage discounts to higher prices.
insights.speaker: Nena Farrell
insights.so_what: Amazon retains demand through promotions while list prices ratchet up.
insights.quote: even if the sales aren't as good as they used to be, since they're similar discounts but on higher prices
insights.locator: But I expect most of those models

insights.claim: The Echo Studio (2nd Gen) at $220 and the Ember Artline TV at $1,099 were the only new Amazon products spared from the August hikes, with Echo Studio held at its original price.
insights.speaker: Nena Farrell
insights.so_what: Amazon held price on premium audio and art-TV products, perhaps to defend share against pricier rivals.

insights.claim: The Ember Artline TV ships with built-in Alexa+, and Amazon prices this art television more accessibly than its more expensive competitors.
insights.speaker: Nena Farrell
insights.so_what: Alexa+ is being bundled into higher-end hardware to push adoption of Amazon's upgraded assistant.

insights.claim: Amazon announced new Kindle versions and a refreshed lineup on the same day the review was published, so buyers choose between discounted current models and preordering new ones.
insights.speaker: Nena Farrell
insights.so_what: Aging models are cleared at discounts while new hardware launches, which may flatter the Prime-event unit count.
insights.locator: So far, most Kindles aren't on sale yet

insights.claim: The reviewer sees the Kindle Colorsoft Kids ($210 after 30% off) as the best Kindle deal, arguing children benefit more from color screens than adults.
insights.speaker: Nena Farrell
insights.so_what: Color e-ink adoption may be driven by children's content and bundled subscriptions rather than adult readers.
insights.quote: I think kids and kids' books have a much better chance of taking advantage of the color screen than adults
